title: Sort by height, chain transfer
summary: Tell three box heights apart with two beams, remember the answer until the box reaches the chain transfer, and send it straight, right or left.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Decide a route from a combination of two sensors.
Remember a decision while the next box is already passing the sensors.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/HeightSortChain.st the inputs and outputs of the line are declared. A press of the start button must run the line. Boxes of three heights arrive on the infeed, nine in all, and the two beams tell the height apart: 0.20 m breaks neither, 0.30 m only BeamLow, 0.40 m both. Every box must end in the bin of its height, none misrouted or dropped, and Done must light when the nine boxes are handled.
stages.checkpoint: Short boxes end in BinShort, medium in BinMedium, tall in BinTall, and Done lights after nine boxes.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, fill a table of the two beams for the three heights. Then follow the first box of the run: when the box stands against the blade, is it still in a beam?
stages.checkpoint: A 0.20 m box breaks neither beam, a 0.30 m box only BeamLow and a 0.40 m box both. The first box has left the beams when EyeChain sees it, about 2.3 s after it entered BeamLow, so at the blade the beams say nothing about it.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Write the program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program drives no output, so no belt moves and no box is sorted. Run the belts after Start, then send each box by its height: straight on, to the right or to the left. Declare whatever else your program needs.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the plant move, press {{ui:toolbar.run.label}} (F5) and open the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named height-sorting-chain and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}: the module stays down for a short box; for the others it stops, rises, slides the box sideways and goes down again. Lift and run are never TRUE together.
stages.checkpoint: MoveRight is TRUE only for medium boxes and MoveLeft only for tall ones, and both only while Lift is TRUE.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The grade sees the three bins and that no box was misrouted or dropped; it does not read your latch, so a wrong answer shows only as a misrouted box.
stages.checkpoint: What the assertions check is tested; nothing else is.

hints.text: Think about when the program needs the height and when the beams can give it: the box leaves the beams before it reaches the blade. What in your program can keep what a beam saw until then?

Latch SawLow and SawHigh whenever Low and High are TRUE, and decide the direction from them once AtBlade has been TRUE for a second (a TON on AtBlade). Clear both latches right after. One state per step: 1 wait for the box, 2 straight on, 3 lift and wait until Raised has held for T#300ms, 4 slide, 5 lower and wait for Lowered. Never run the module while Lift is TRUE.

faultCases: The starting program drives no output, so no belt moves and no box is sorted.
